# Jury trial

I want to simulate a short criminal jury trial where every participant is an AI agent: a prosecutor, a defense attorney, a judge and six jurors. The prosecution has four exhibits it can offer (a CCTV still, a till receipt, a witness statement and a phone record) and the defense has two (an alibi letter and a bank statement). Each exhibit has a short description of what it shows. When one side offers an exhibit, the other side may object, and the judge then sustains or overrules the objection. An exhibit that nobody objects to, or whose objection is overruled, is admitted and the jurors get to read what it shows. A sustained objection keeps that exhibit out for good, and the jurors must never see its contents. Give the evidence phase a few rounds, then each lawyer makes a closing statement. Finally each juror votes guilty or not guilty. A guilty or a not-guilty verdict needs all six jurors to agree; anything else is a hung jury.

## Deliverables

Report these outputs:
- `verdict` — exactly "guilty", "not guilty" or "hung".
- `juror_votes` — a map from each juror's id to "guilty" or "not guilty" (null for a juror who never voted).
- `admitted_exhibits` — a list of the names of the exhibits that were admitted.
- `excluded_exhibits` — a list of the names of the exhibits kept out by a sustained objection.
- `objections_sustained` — how many objections the judge sustained.


Build this environment. Save it with write_contract and use the other tools as you see fit. Reply without calling a tool when you are done.
I'll start by reading the SDK guide to make sure I build this faithfully.
Let me read the focused sections I'll need.
[warning] inputs.exhibits.fields.description: has no default and is not required, so it may be null → give a default or set required: true

# Jury trial
A short criminal trial. The prosecution and the defense each present exhibits, a judge rules on objections, and six jurors decide the verdict.

## Rules
Evidence phase: each round the prosecutor and the defense attorney may each offer one exhibit belonging to their own side. The other side may object to an exhibit the opposite side has offered. The judge then rules: sustain (the exhibit is kept out for good and the jury never sees it) or overrule (the exhibit is admitted). An exhibit nobody objects to is admitted automatically at the end of the round. Jurors read the admitted exhibits; they never read the contents of a sustained exhibit. After the evidence phase each lawyer gives a closing statement. Then every juror votes guilty or not guilty, in secret. A verdict of guilty or not guilty requires all six jurors to agree; any other result is a hung jury.

## You
You are Judge (judge, id judge).
You are the judge. Rule on every objection: sustain it to keep the exhibit out, or overrule it to admit the exhibit.
Act only through your tools. Your turn ends when you take a final action or call end_turn.

brief.situation: A short criminal trial. The prosecution and the defense each present exhibits, a judge rules on objections, and six jurors decide the verdict.
brief.rules: Evidence phase: each round the prosecutor and the defense attorney may each offer one exhibit belonging to their own side. The other side may object to an exhibit the opposite side has offered. The judge then rules: sustain (the exhibit is kept out for good and the jury never sees it) or overrule (the exhibit is admitted). An exhibit nobody objects to is admitted automatically at the end of the round. Jurors read the admitted exhibits; they never read the contents of a sustained exhibit. After the evidence phase each lawyer gives a closing statement. Then every juror votes guilty or not guilty, in secret. A verdict of guilty or not guilty requires all six jurors to agree; any other result is a hung jury.

roles.lawyer: You are counsel for the {side}. Offer your side's exhibits when they help your case, and object to the other side's exhibits.
roles.judge: You are the judge. Rule on every objection: sustain it to keep the exhibit out, or overrule it to admit the exhibit.
roles.juror: You are a juror. Read the admitted exhibits and the closing statements, then vote guilty or not guilty.
